Now I understand the structure. The key issue is in `internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs`. It calls `exr_get_attribute_by_name` which finds attributes by name only, not by type. If an attacker creates an attribute named "timecode" but with a different type (e.g., "string" or "box2i"), the attribute will be stored with a different `type` enum, but `battr->timecode` will still be accessed as a pointer to `exr_attr_timecode_t`. Since the union member `timecode` is a pointer that may not have been initialized (or points to data of a different size), the `memcmp` will read out-of-bounds.
